texts.preamble: Ravindra Bhagwanshingh Sabale vs The State Of Maharashtra on 24 November, 2025 Author: Madhav J. Jamdar Bench: Madhav J. Jamdar 2025:Bhc-As:51040 603-Aba-543-202 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction Anticipatory Bail Application No.543 Of 2023 Ravindra B. Sabale ...Applican Versus The State of Maharashtra ...Responde Mr. Sachin B. Chandan, for the Applicant. Ms. R.V. Newton, App, for the Respondent-State. Mr. Dinesh Parashram, Police Naik, attached to Jaykheda Police Station, Nashik (Rural), present. Coram: Madhav J. Jamdar, J. Dated : 24th November 2025 Pc:-
texts.facts: 2. By the present Application, the Applicant is seeking pre- arrest bail in connection with C.R. No.356 of 2022 registered on 14th December 2022 with Jaykheda Police Station, District Nashik (Rural) under Sections 188, 179, 272, 273, 328 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC") and for the offence Ravindra Bhagwanshingh Sabale vs The State Of Maharashtra on 24 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55312228/ 1 punishable under Sections 26(2)(i), 3(1)(zz)(iv), 26(2)(iv) and Page 1 As per the prosecution case the Applicant was dealing with contraband material which is unsafe and dangerous for the health of people. 4. It is the submission of Mr. Sachin Chandan, learned Counsel that except the offence under Section 328 of IPC, all other offences are bailable offences.
texts.arguments: He submits that as far as Section 328 of IPC is concerned, the Supreme Court is considering the applicability of Section 328 of IPC to the similar cases. He therefore, states that the Anticipatory Bail be granted. 5. On the other hand, Ms. Newton, learned APP strongly opposes the Anticipatory Bail Application. She submits that the offence is very serious and therefore, the Anticipatory Bail Application be rejected. She submits that there is one antecedent being C.R. No.356 of 2022 registered for the offence punishable Ravindra Bhagwanshingh Sabale vs The State Of Maharashtra on 24 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55312228/ 2 under Sections 328, 272, 273, 179, 188 and read with 34 of IPC and for the offence punishable under Sections 26(2)(i), 3(1)(z)(v), Page 2 ::: Uploaded on - 25/11/2025 ::: Downloaded on - 26/11/2025 20:38:14 ::: 603-ABA-543-2023.ODT Akash Tayde 26(2)(4) and under Section 59 of the FSSA with Jaykheda Police Station, District Nashik (Rural). 6. Learned APP submits that if this Court is inclined to grant Anticipatory Bail then the Applicant be directed to give undertaking in terms of order of the Supreme Court in the case of Abhijit Jitendra Lolage vs State of Maharashtra 1 and more particularly relies on following condition imposed by the Supreme Court in case of similar offences :- "It is deemed appropriate to impose the condition - "I, Abhijeet Jitendra Lolage do undertake to not deal with Gutkha, that is, Pan Masala with Tobacco". In case, the appellant - Abhijeet Jitendra Lolage violates the terms and conditions of bail, including the undertaking imposed, it would be open to the prosecution to seek cancellation of bail ". (Emphasis added) Mr. Sachin Chandan, learned Counsel appearing for the Applicant Ravindra Bhagwanshingh Sabale vs The State Of Maharashtra on 24 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55312228/ 3 after taking the instructions submits that the Applicant will give the undertaking. 1 SLP (Crl.)
